title: Towards Weakly-Supervised Hate Speech Classification Across Datasets
measurement_description: The paper evaluates weakly-supervised methods for classifying hate speech targeting specific religious groups, namely Muslims and Jews, in both in-dataset and cross-dataset settings.
findings: The study found that its weakly-supervised model (X-Class) could effectively classify hate speech against Jewish and Muslim groups, achieving comparable performance in cross-dataset scenarios as in in-dataset ones for these categories. The performance was partly attributed to the fact that the source dataset's 'Racist' category was heavily skewed towards content about Muslims and Jews, providing relevant data for the fine-grained target categories.
